summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of liver transplant, chronic kidney disease, and prior cholangitis was admitted with a two-day history of fevers and generalized myalgias. He had no respiratory or gastrointestinal symptoms and was initially found to have mild pulmonary vascular congestion on chest imaging, but no acute infection. Blood and urine cultures were negative, and respiratory viral testing showed no evidence of influenza or other common viruses. His mental status, which was briefly altered on admission, improved with fever resolution. The clinical course was consistent with a self-limited viral syndrome. He remained afebrile for over 24 hours, and was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue immunosuppressive therapy and follow up with the transplant clinic, including a planned ERCP in the coming months.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage I through stage IV, or unspecified
